evidence_map_additions.value: The account describes funding-cut orders; implementation and enforcement outcomes are not established.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Trump signed executive orders directing cuts to federal funding for NPR, PBS, and local public broadcasters, citing alleged bias.

evidence_map_additions.value: A federal judge found Arpaio guilty of criminal contempt; Trump pardoned him before sentencing.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: On July 31, 2017, U.S. District Judge Susan Bolton found former Maricopa County sheriff Joe Arpaio guilty of criminal contempt after a five-day bench trial.

evidence_map_additions.value: The DOJ record confirms a commutation but does not state the replacement sentence or whether supervised release changed.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney records a commutation for Dwayne Phelps on January 19, 2021.

evidence_map_additions.value: UAE authorities reported aerial threats and interception activity in cumulative regional totals.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The UAE figures are attributed to its defense authorities and describe the running totals as of the report, not a one-day count for March 3.

evidence_map_additions.value: Representative Robert Garcia sent a congressional letter asking the Justice Department to account for withheld Epstein-related files; the response and disposition were not yet reported.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Representative Robert Garcia sent Attorney General Pam Bondi a letter demanding a full accounting of Epstein-related files that had not appeared in the Justice Department’s public release, according to The Guardian.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump announced planned attendance at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner; the announcement itself did not establish increased press access or fuller war briefings.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The Associated Press reported on March 3, 2026, that Donald Trump said he would attend the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, a break with the practice of his first term.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump announced a ten-day ceasefire due to begin on April 16, 2026; the BBC described it as an opening for negotiations, not a final settlement.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Trump announced a ten-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon after six weeks of fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump publicly endorsed Senator Tim Scott for reelection in 2022; the endorsement was not a campaign result or a guarantee about primary opposition.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Donald Trump publicly endorsed Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina for reelection in 2022 on March 2, 2021.

evidence_map_additions.value: Elon Musk announced America PAC to support Trump’s presidential campaign; the PAC later promoted a website that collected contact details.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: In the fall, the PAC promoted a website that offered election-related information and sought users’ contact details.

evidence_map_additions.value: Employees described questioning by White House visitors about qualifications and political views; the account does not identify every visitor or the fate of every employee.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The linked account says the visitors asked about qualifications and political views while often declining to identify themselves.

evidence_map_additions.value: The SEC closed its Robinhood investigation without an enforcement action and gave no public reason in the supplied account.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The agency did not publicly explain its decision in the report summarized here.

evidence_map_additions.value: Elon Musk announced an all-stock sale of X to his artificial-intelligence company xAI.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: On March 28, 2025, Elon Musk announced on X that he had sold the social-media platform, formerly known as Twitter, to xAI, his artificial-intelligence company.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump commented on reports of a possible Russian-involved breach of a U.S. court system; the supplied account does not confirm attribution or identify the affected court.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: On August 13, 2025, Donald Trump responded to media reports suggesting Russian involvement in a breach of a U.S. court system with a characteristically dismissive remark:

evidence_map_additions.value: The administration directed the Park Service to remove or revise historical materials; completed changes at individual sites are not established.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The Trump administration directed the National Park Service to remove or revise materials at historic sites that it said “inappropriately disparage Americans,” following a March 2025 executive order.

evidence_map_additions.value: The White House excluded AP journalists from the press pool; after a federal judge ruled for AP, a revised policy continued limiting access.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The White House began excluding Associated Press journalists from the presidential press pool on February 11, 2025, after the AP declined to change its style guide to call the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America.”

evidence_map_additions.value: Buyers filed a civil complaint alleging that sales claims were overstated; the filing did not establish fraud or knowing deception.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: In August 2010, buyers of units in the Trump SoHo hotel-condominium project filed a civil complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump declared a national economic emergency under IEEPA as preparation for the April 2 tariff announcement; legal challenges and statutory validity remained unresolved.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: In late March 2025, President Donald Trump invoked the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), declaring a national economic emergency tied to trade imbalances.

evidence_map_additions.value: Tom Price resigned after scrutiny of official travel; Trump said he was unhappy and accepted the resignation.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Price resigned on September 29 after the travel drew sustained scrutiny.

evidence_map_additions.value: Truth Social launched with technical problems and a waitlist; the supplied account also describes a separate open-source licensing dispute.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The supplied account says hundreds of thousands of users remained on a waitlist for months and that, upon release, the app received the lowest ratings of any app in Apple’s App Store.

evidence_map_additions.value: Mar-a-Lago raised its membership fee after Trump’s 2016 election victory and later hosted presidential visits and government meetings; the account does not establish pay-to-play or a particular policy purchase.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Shortly after Trump’s 2016 election victory, Mar-a-Lago raised its membership fee from $100,000 to $200,000.

evidence_map_additions.value: Trump posted about the Army anniversary parade before an official announcement, and the account says Defense Department communications were adjusted; it documents no concrete threat or classified disclosure.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The record says the post included operational details and prompted the Defense Department to adjust communications procedures.

evidence_map_additions.value: Clark drafted an unshared letter to Georgia officials, while senior DOJ officials opposed appointing him acting attorney general and threatened to resign.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: Clark drafted a letter to Georgia officials promoting false concerns about the election.

evidence_map_additions.value: The Trump administration announced that the United States would withdraw from UNESCO; the announcement did not immediately end every U.S. connection with its programs.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: On October 12, 2017, the Trump administration announced that the United States would withdraw from UNESCO, the United Nations agency working across education, science, and culture.

evidence_map_additions.value: The report described Treasury withholding money from the 9/11 victims fund; it did not establish denied or delayed care or whether the funds were later distributed.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: The New York Daily News reported on September 11, 2020, that the Treasury Department had withheld around $3.2 million from a fund for 9/11 victims.

evidence_map_additions.value: A federal judge found that USPS violated an existing injunction by issuing an election-mail rule but declined to block the rule at that stage.
evidence_map_additions.basis_quote: On August 25, 2026, a federal judge found that the Postal Service violated an existing injunction when it issued a new election-mail rule.
